event: Nala holds very still and strains to hear the low voices beyond the walls.
prose: You hold very still, as still as a body this small can be, and strain to make out what the voices beyond the walls are saying.

event: Three voices: her mother's, close and soft; a man's and a woman's, farther off and duller.
prose: There are three of them. One voice is close and soft, and it hums through the walls around you as much as it reaches you through them: the woman you are inside, your mother. The other two are farther off and duller, a man's voice and a woman's.

event: The man does most of the talking, slow and pleased; the woman cuts in short now and then.
prose: The man does most of the talking. He takes his time over it, and he sounds pleased. Now and then the woman cuts in, short and dry, and he goes on.

event: Not one word is English; the sounds run together in a tongue she has never heard.
prose: You listen for English and don't hear a word of it. The sounds run together in a language you have never heard, all soft consonants and long, rolling vowels, with breaks in the wrong places.

event: One word comes back again and again, the same two sounds each time: kerith.
prose: But one word keeps coming back. The man says it, then your mother, then the man again, the same two sounds each time. Kerith.

event: The rest slips past her; she gets the shape and mood of the talk, never its sense.
prose: The rest slips past you. You can follow the shape of the talk, when a question goes up at its end and when an answer comes down flat, and you can tell they are pleased with something. What any of it means, you can't tell at all.

event: Window: New Path - Path of Eavesdropping.

changes.note: New Path shown: Path of Eavesdropping

event: Her mother says something soft; the man laughs, and the woman says kerith again.
A heavy hand presses on the wall beside her: the man's, laid flat on her mother's belly.
The talk stops. All three fall quiet, the hand still pressing, as if waiting on her.
